subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config/API shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix adds public configuration surface and changes how high-risk tools can be hidden from a requester while remaining available to spawned children.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented `selfDeny`/`delegateOnly`-style field with deny precedence, inherited-policy tests, effective-tool diagnostics, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Reject new core surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or prompt-level delegation as the supported pattern, accepting that config-enforced separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented `selfDeny`/`delegateOnly`-style field with deny precedence, inherited-policy tests, effective-tool diagnostics, and ACP/runtime behavior explicitly defined.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent gateway/subagent policy history and prior maintainer-facing review make this the strongest available owner signal for the security-boundary choice.
